job: Treating the artifact gap as the explicit optimization target via rubric-targeted post-training on artifact-bearing tasks rather than larger context windows
outcome: A named GPT-Rosalind-successor or scientific-agent system reporting a sub-10-point LifeSciBench artifact-vs-text spread at or above current overall accuracy
motivation: The artifact gap is the cleanest, most-cited objection a lab can move, and quantifying its shrinkage is the precondition before anyone trusts the agent with real experimental data

task.what: Post-train an agent to lift artifact-task accuracy toward its text-only level
task.where: On LifeSciBench or a comparably artifact-grounded successor benchmark
task.when: A reported result landing by H2 2027, with training runs through 2026 into 2027
task.why: The 17-point artifact cliff is the single most-cited weakness blocking trust
task.how: Rubric-targeted RL on artifact-bearing tasks plus file-aware tool use

job: Shipping native readers and file-aware tools for genomic sequence, chemical-structure, and raw-assay formats so an agent can parse the data objects a working scientist manipulates
outcome: A robust agent-callable toolset that ingests sequence/structure/experimental-data files and URLs without the agent falling back to prose reasoning
motivation: Tool-and-parser grounding is the tractable mechanism that converts a fluent-in-prose model into one that handles real data objects

task.who: the bioinformatics and cheminformatics tooling maintainer team
task.what: Build native parsers and file-aware tool wrappers for scientific artifacts
task.where: In open-source bio/chem libraries and the agent tool-calling layer
task.when: Rolling releases through 2026 ahead of the H2 2027 landing
task.why: Native artifact readers are the direct lever against the measured failure
task.how: Format-specific readers exposed as structured, file-aware agent tools

job: Maintaining and extending LifeSciBench so it keeps both text-only and real-artifact task tracks that isolate and quantify the gap as an optimization target
outcome: A live, accepted benchmark that separately scores artifact and text tasks, letting any submission report a comparable sub-10-point spread
motivation: A standing artifact-vs-text split turns the most-cited objection into a tracked, falsifiable number labs can compete to shrink

task.who: the LifeSciBench (or successor benchmark) maintainer team
task.what: Keep a paired artifact-task and text-only track that measures the gap
task.where: On the public LifeSciBench leaderboard and its successor evaluations
task.when: Sustained through 2026 and 2027 so H2 2027 submissions are comparable
task.why: A stable artifact split is needed for the gap claim to be falsifiable
task.how: Curating artifact-bearing tasks and reporting artifact and text scores separately
